findings.evidence: Norm/Order.lean:88 `orderOfVanishingAt_le_orderOfVanishingAt_norm` (only the `≤` form is public; its docstring already says 'the zeros of the norm dominate the zeros of the form'); OfVanishing.lean:146 `orderOfVanishingAt_nonneg`; roadmap ModularForms/README.md:337-338 names exactly this step.
findings.fix: Add a public lemma to `Norm/Order.lean` beside `orderOfVanishingAt_le_orderOfVanishingAt_norm`, e.g. `orderOfVanishingAt_norm_ne_zero (f : F) {p : ℍ} (h : orderOfVanishingAt (⇑f) p ≠ 0) : orderOfVanishingAt (⇑(ModularForm.norm ℋ f)) p ≠ 0`, list it in that file's Main declarations, and reduce lines 205–207 to a call to it.
findings.issue: The reusable step — `orderOfVanishingAt f p ≠ 0 → orderOfVanishingAt (⇑(ModularForm.norm ℋ f)) p ≠ 0`, general in `ℋ` — is proved inline here from `orderOfVanishingAt_nonneg` + `orderOfVanishingAt_le_orderOfVanishingAt_norm`. `Norm/Order.lean` exposes only the `≤` form, so every consumer of the roadmap's 'zeros of Nm(f) dominate those of f' must redo this; the PR description reports #3330 already re-proving it as a private lemma.

findings.evidence: Orbits.lean:196-199: `𝒢` absent from `Set.Finite (Quotient.mk'' '' {p | orderOfVanishingAt f p ≠ 0})` and from `hf`. Contrast Norm/Order.lean:61-64, where `orderOfVanishingAt_norm`'s conclusion mentions `ℋ ⧸ 𝒢.subgroupOf ℋ`, and FiniteZeros.lean:60, which fixes the literal `𝒮ℒ`. No in-repo call site exercises the new lemma.
findings.fix: Make the group explicit — `(𝒢 : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ))` before the instance binders — as `ModularForm.norm ℋ f` does, or otherwise ensure `[ModularFormClass F 𝒢 k]` precedes `[𝒢.IsFiniteRelIndex 𝒮ℒ]`.
findings.issue: `{𝒢 : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ)}` (and `k`) occur in no explicit argument and in no part of the conclusion — only in `[𝒢.IsFiniteRelIndex 𝒮ℒ]` and `[ModularFormClass F 𝒢 k]`, with the relative-index instance listed before the class that would pin `𝒢` down. The level is then picked solely by instance search on an unconstrained metavariable, and a user cannot name the level at the call site without `(𝒢 := ·)`.

summary: The added surface is free of compatibility artifacts and exposed bodies, but it inlines the one genuinely reusable general-level step (nonzero order dominated under the norm) instead of exposing it in Norm/Order.lean, and its group parameter 𝒢 appears only inside instance binders, so the level is never nameable in the statement.
